meta.title: mini-loop Runtime Architecture
meta.subtitle: Python runtime in python/; independent Go startup, owned HTTP/SSE, guarded turns and per-run JSONL; session persistence/optional port work remains

views.label: One agent turn
views.note: Follow an authenticated request through owner binding into one serialized session and out to the model provider.

views.label: Guarded tool execution
views.note: Tools cross the permission gate. Optional decisions return typed judgments from Jev or an explicitly selected LLM, without acting.

views.label: Optional orchestration
views.note: Background, cron, teams, subagents, and the default-off workflow runtime feed later session turns.

views.label: Go port in progress
views.note: Optional decision gate: masked state, Jev or isolated LLM, shared model limits. Goals restore disarmed; SQL pending.

views.label: Capture a personal skill
views.note: Follow the authenticated-turn ledger, explicit user commit, durable owner file, and next-session activation without live rebinding.

components.label: Go managed cron
components.tag: cron tools opt-in; arm is operator

cards.title: Concurrency
items: One lock serializes each session
Fleet-wide LLM and tool semaphores bound parallel work
Parallel-safe tool results retain model-call order

cards.title: Trust
items: Authority is stamped before resources are resolved
Only authenticated HTTP user/final turns enter preview
Preview cannot publish; commit is a separate caller action
Agent and user skills retain explicit provenance

cards.title: Durability boundary
items: Pending personal-skill drafts are capped, expiring, and process-local
Committed owner skills and memory are durable local files, not SQLite rows
Publication is create-only and activates in future sessions

cards.title: Typed decisions
items: Off by default, including the full feature bundle
Explicit state + batch choice / score / noul questions
External-risk approval; judgments never execute actions
Jev values retain provenance; LLM estimates are labeled

cards.title: Language layout
items: The main map follows the Python runtime under python/
Go NewRuntimeSession registers ten implemented tools behind one typed gate
SessionManager owns ManagedSession admission/cancel/status and drains scratch cleanup; raw children emit core spans only
Skill source digests are rechecked; questions return text or an unanswered variant
Go requests consume fitted schemas, skills and optional scoped memory; archives are workspace files
Go children use capability-selected tools, fresh state and peer provenance
Optional Go journals replay terminal results; SQLite backend remains pending
Optional bound approvals preserve grants, text answers, reviewer abstention and typed rows; no SQLite backend yet
Optional registry masking precedes result settlement and covers implemented events, approvals and compaction files; live arguments stay raw
Real host shell consumes selected credentials, bounds shared capture, masks streams and kills process groups; Seatbelt and future sink coverage remain open
Default cache uses detached wire annotations; stuck detection keeps 20 steps and nudges once before halting
Children inherit typed prompt/injector seams, cache/stuck policies and exact model/tool pools with fresh state
Parallel groups preserve result/step order; exclusive tools are barriers and bypass tool permits
Manager shares model/tool pools of eight; bare model calls are unbounded
Todo reminder counters survive user turns; durable steering, restore and remaining context integrations remain open
Typed events replay 200 records; live queues shed oldest at 2,000; sinks receive masked detached records
Transcript rewrites open event epochs; bounded HTTP SSE replay exists, durable cursor gap recovery remains pending
Go HTTP handler admits one principal, twenty-eight route operations and masked JSON/SSE data; optional UI APIs and full posture remain open
Managed control queues inject bounded steering and operator posture before context budgeting; permission mode is read after before/guard hooks
HTTP idle steering publishes an owned background turn; manager deletion/shutdown joins it, children never drain parent controls

Fork copies completed paired history into fresh scratch; typed lineage and source events are process-local, configured state injection flushes fork history before publication; native SQLite remains pending
Explicit direct HTTP provider preserves typed cache wire, served model and signed thinking; typed SSE assembly and SDK retries are separate from default Agent recovery

Provider byte caps, caller-owned deadlines/waits, credential-scrubbed diagnostics and redirect refusal are implemented; configurable coalesced masked progress is ephemeral and cancellation preserves shown text; outer waits release permits; fallback and paired reactive shrink are session-owned; production conformance remains unverified
Go fake clients own call IDs, signed thinking, typed responders and explicit direct/stream views; child and fork sessions retain captured progress thresholds
The Go entry node includes cmd/miniloop and launcher: typed settings, activation checks, requested/actual bind guards, owned TCP listener and joined signal shutdown
All 49 Python settings are typed; 64 source cases compare defaults, overrides and refusal. Embedded default skill matches Python and needs no checkout

Default per-run trajectory JSONL is enabled; a private spill.Store is best-effort configured by default. String Bash preserves masked captures; actual structured defaults bypass it in Python and Go. Compaction artifacts are separate
Dump-config reports credential-free settings/availability without files or model probes; full posture, dotenv discovery, optional UI data, durable SQLite and optional services remain pending

Typed ManagerServices/RuntimeConfig spill binding retains credential scope and process tracking; hashed workspace namespaces are grouping, not ACLs. Exclusive private leaves do not confine parent races; no TTL/purge, and shutdown retains evidence
Go SessionManager aggregates the per-run file service: ordered masked full fields stay outside the live backlog; terminal finish precedes live persistence receipts
Four owned trajectory list/inspect/export operations read retained files after deletion/restart; JSON caps eight MiB, JSONL streams without client-held append locks
Explicit library purge joins writers first; file evidence has no session restore, fsync guarantee, cross-process lease or host ACL. HTML viewer and operator CLI preserve source CSS/JS and typed rows
Go entry aggregates the independent traceview CLI/renderer: span pairs, child depth, request numbering, unknown rows, real timing and bounded inspectors
Owned HTML reads use the eight-MiB source ceiling. The offline CLI renders exports or session chronology to 0600 files; no HTTP principal or restore authority is invented
Filtered VisitRecords yields detached wire bytes without client-held append locks; limit counts yielded records and may scan the whole file
Go entry also embeds public console/UI shells from the Python source: no static mount or runtime checkout, while data requests retain authentication
Go Resources aggregates explicit TaskTools: five typed graph tools, masked atomic workspace records, dependency gates and exclusive owner markers; comprehensive feature activation remains unsupported
Owned Tasks HTTP reads admit session ownership before fresh store access and do not consume claims. Orphan markers report for operator repair; no leases or host ACLs
Browser core create/send/tool/final/trajectory flows are verified; optional Team/Goal/Workflows/Skills/Memory/Improve/Benchmark/Audit pane APIs remain pending

Explicit go/worktrees service creates/binds/keeps/removes Git worktrees and appends audit events; Go Resources also installs five model tools only with WorktreeTools=true, through the common risk/permission gate

enter_worktree is an exclusive barrier: prepare files, shell/sandbox, model context, approval/question surfaces and future children before publishing execution scope; manager Info, task HTTP roots, trajectory attribution and scratch cleanup retain the original lifecycle workspace

An initialized task board stays pinned; first lazy task admission after entry uses the new execution workspace. Fresh children use current files/shell but do not borrow the manager worktree service; selected worktree tools report unconfigured. Forks retain manager activation with fresh scratch
Shell rebind retains deadline, capture, secrets, spill and foreground interrupt ownership; custom factories must report the target root. OS sandbox backend and full feature activation remain pending

Go SessionManager aggregates an explicit WorktreeWorkspaceFactory adapter to go/worktrees: factory provisioning is independent of model-tool activation and paths are scratch, including plain-directory fallback

Actual Python and Go delete drain shared holders then remove even dirty factory directories, leaving Git registration and branch; stop, PreserveWorkspace and explicit bound admission retain work. Guarded worktree Remove is separate
The existing Go failed-admission cleanup removes unpublished scratch without Git metadata cleanup; Python create instead leaves the allocation. Source has no Git-aware manager reclaimer

Go shell node aggregates background.NewWithExecutor and the explicit RuntimeConfig.BackgroundTools library flag: fresh per-session lazy state shares native argv/credentials/sandbox, with distinct merged-byte capture. Two model tools use the same gate

Background .background records mask commands, atomically record in-flight evidence and report orphan/PID liveness without replay or ownership. CancelAll returns joinable cancelled handles; Close joins them. Caller owns admission quiescence and later Run is allowed

Background retains 100 full results, lists/projects newest 50 and preserves undrained notifications; metadata/undrained queue remain unbounded. Future rebind pins admitted executors and original ledger root. Go cleans pre-start cancellation where Python leaves Running/ledger

Background completion queues feed Go Session before model requests: optional background_run/check_background and conditional Bash dispatch/classification share the gate; bounded task_notification injection emits typed background_result events. Interruption markers name live survivors; prepared background scopes follow workspace entry. Manager delete/stop join lazy service ownership after turn drain, before scratch cleanup; forks get fresh state/root. Standalone --background-tools selects this individual service; the comprehensive feature bundle stays unsupported. Explicitly selected child scopes use independent qualified IDs/queues and remain owned through return; root cleanup cancels/joins descendants. Root adopts existing evidence before child admission; no child adopts live parent records. Qualified child orphans remain reportable after restart. Metadata/queues are unbounded and cross-process/shared-session ledger arbitration remains absent

Go SessionManager owns cron by default: owner-scoped schedule/list/cancel/arm, fresh untrusted scheduled turns and deletion/stop joins. Three explicit CronTools model variants cross the common gate via a typed CronControl; Arm is operator-only. Go Resources aggregates the bound handlers. Four owned HTTP operations work without tool activation; --cron-tools selects model tools alone. Forks retain activation with fresh jobs; selected children remain unconfigured. Standalone startup retains restored disarmed state, mark-before-dispatch and minute claims. Missing cron handles now resolve lazily inside the owned cancellation context: bound paths are retained, scratch uses the current factory, recorded owner/history is restored and a fresh untrusted turn follows explicit arm. Stop cancels cooperative restore reads and joins. Snapshot 47 compares seven actual Python scheduled restores plus the next request. Missing SQL rows cannot claim and remain anonymous/unconfirmed; no-store fallback is ephemeral. Scheduled system uses the current builder, matching source. Native SQLite restart proof, strict 422 detail parity and comprehensive feature activation remain pending; stale JSON writers and external exactly-once effects remain outside the claim protocol.

Go schema-v7 StateStore now optionally binds managed sessions and manager default journal/approval rows to an injected backend. Pre-request transcript guards, masked event-first capture, rewrite epochs and separate process leases are implemented. Claims occur after admission; confirmed renewal loss cancels the turn. Steering saves before acknowledgment; delete disables writes before row removal/cancellation, and stop releases leases after drain. Ordinary write faults degrade and are reported; count/query invariants stop requests. Renewal and metadata refresh require growth, not a heartbeat; status can remain running after completion. Snapshot 45 compares actual Python AgentSession/SQLite recipes through a test-only Go backend. Explicit manager RestoreSessions now rebuilds recorded facts and highest-epoch references; claims precede approval expiry and crash-tail repair. Foreign-held handles remain pending, and turn admission reloads latest rows after claim. Todo/steering survive repair, payload sequences are not reused, and stop joins restoration without late publication. Snapshot 46 captures actual Python manager/SQLite differences; Go tests the first resumed request and failure/shutdown paths through a test backing. Injected-store bounded SSE catch-up and transcript epoch reads are implemented. Native SQLite/backend/restart and state-backend launcher activation remain pending. Typed goals now fold snapshots with disarmed activation. Plan-mode boolean archival decoding and log folding now restore prompt guidance without authority. Archival decoding restores no actor/capabilities or broker grants. Plan validation/review refusals are completed textual outcomes with failed=false; callback/hook faults remain failed. Snapshot 52 compares observers, journal, stuck steps, model results, recordings and replay.

Go goal tools are explicit; the default stateless stop consumer consumes bounded continuations. Create/resume require explicit human provenance; logged goal restoration is always disarmed; SQL remains pending.

Explicit Go decision tools use the external-risk gate, mask and revalidate supplied state, and share model limits. Jev preserves provenance; independent LLM queries omit parent history/tools/cache/streams and reject partial replies before recovery can continue. Typed metadata and private inputs share existing event/trajectory sinks. Closed result strings and member names are masked before escaping, including backend model values; nested results stay masked in journals, state and recordings. Cooperative cancellation settles cancelled actions and releases model permits. Launcher settings select llm/jev with explicit backend precedence; offline reports omit credentials. Full source replay audit remains pending.

Go userresources now provides an explicit operator DirectoryResolver: exact owner digest paths, 0700 root/skills/memory directories, planted child-link refusal and immutable cached bindings. Filesystem libraries aggregates it with workspace backends; operator binding does not cross the model gate. Go skills also provides explicit agent/user LayeredCatalog snapshots: collision refusal, combined budget and shared source verification. Go memory provides explicit typed Markdown Store/ScopedStore: exact owner keys, scoped replacement, lazy cache/index, lexical search and masked atomic writes. An explicit userresources Resolver now caches immutable complete owner bundles with separate skill logs and bound memory; failed construction is uncached and retries recheck directories. The native durable library now supplies component-wise no-follow descriptors, bounded regular reads and fsynced no-replace hard-link creation as the publication file boundary. Catalog.WithSourceDocument prepares detached path-ordered entries before commit using the same bounded parser, independent diagnostics and full source verification; it does not write files or grant publication authority. Operator Resolver.PublishSkill now screens raw fields and registry health, prepares safe typed receipts/catalogues before create-only link commit, verifies bounded exact retries and replaces only future-resolution cache bundles while retaining live snapshots/memory. Synthetic prepared entries retain full source verification. Custom maskers without a typed registration surface fail closed; registered values require health reporting. Explicit ManagerServices.UserResources now resolves trusted owners before new/forked/restored session construction. Optional ManagerServices.Memory supplies one shared Store when no resolver is configured; the same create/fork/ordinary and scheduled restore map binds the admitted owner. Resolver errors refuse admission without fallback. Files and the Store lifecycle lock retain their existing ownership; binding alone leaves memory tools default-off. Standalone startup now always constructs shared storage at the configured memory root or WorkspaceRoot/.memory, then optional private owner resource root; both must succeed before manager publication. Open-bind refusal precedes filesystem effects. --memory-tools selects remember/recall, --memory-auto=false disables automatic selection/capture; defaults carry storage without memory tools. Pure Inspect/dump reports backend/tool/auto selection without creating roots or model calls. RuntimeConfig.UserResources copies and validates complete owner-matching bundles before filesystem effects, selecting the layered source. Live sessions and native selected children retain snapshots; forks resolve the current cache and deletion preserves owner files. Builtin skill-domain refusals carry a named error and render completed source text outcomes; custom backend/cancellation faults remain errors. Source teammate inheritance is compared through the native binding seam, not a native teammate scheduler. Explicit MemoryTools now installs typed remember/recall through the common gate with write/read risk and exclusive execution. Scoped owner stores are checked before workspace effects; resource bundles take precedence, selected children retain the store, and no model owner/root override exists. Explicit remember now holds a Store-owned process-local lifecycle lock shared across scoped bindings; cancellable waiting and deferred release preserve ordinary scoped operations through a separate operation lock. Independent Store instances remain independent; there is no cross-process fencing or rollback. The memory extraction stage now strips recalled/runtime context and tool-result bodies, uses the source ASCII JSON tail and first-five incremental owner writes. Its agent_turn side request has explicit non-live history ownership and leaves the live token meter unchanged. Automatic capture now holds this lifecycle across extraction and consolidation after normal final text, stop-hook continuation stuck halt and round exhaustion. Tool-pair/auto/writable checks admit it; readonly, disabled, missing pair, provider-error and cancellation exits skip it. The actual source tool-batch stuck halt omits capture and remains unchanged. At ten records, a 2500-token memory_consolidation non-live request replaces only bound-owner records, preserving unchanged origins. Ordinary capture faults emit bounded masked memory_capture_error and retain the completed result; cancellation and native transcript/lease failures propagate. Typed memory/extract and capture-error events detach and support informational archival reads. Recall uses five-record lexical search and source provenance wrappers; store and gate masking protect their separate sinks. Default role capabilities omit the tools. With both memory tools selected, automatic selection defaults on with a copied MemoryAuto=false override. A 200-token normal side request uses the rewritten input tail and scoped catalogue, preserving source model/recovery/limiter/cache events without observing the live meter. Ordered integer/boolean indices select provenance blocks; errors or empty selections use lexical fallback, while cancellation and native state authority failures propagate. Typed memory/load events survive archival decoding without authority. Changed runtime facts expose a nonempty scoped index only with recall, independent of the auto flag. The explicit native DraftStore operator library now retains immutable owner/session-bound records with typed evidence/coverage, FIFO 64/16/4 quotas, fifteen-minute TTL, constant-time digest checks and detached public previews. Wrong authority returns absence before expiry/digest; global capacity never evicts foreign owners. Consume is atomic; post-publication cleanup uses exact identity and ignores elapsed TTL. Separate pure native skill projection helpers now preserve admitted text or filter legacy protocol history, strip recalled memory greedily, discard complete user arrays, mark excluded compaction and mask fixed display strings/keys before whole-message suffix budgeting under compact Unicode Python JSON capped at 40k. Python Unicode 14 word boundaries are pinned. Display labels confer no role or provenance. ManagedSession now owns a fresh process-local CaptureLedger and records trimmed input/final pairs only after successful terminal flush with the trusted personal_skill.capture_source capability. HTTP admission stamps it; ordinary, peer and cron calls do not inherit it. Masking covers display strings and keys before source 64-message/40k Unicode JSON bounds, with oldest-message eviction and exact omission counts. Plain history gap markers latch excluded compaction. Secret screening failures refuse append and latch preview refusal even after registry recovery; capture faults cannot fail completed turns. Snapshots detach; restored and forked history cannot mint evidence. This overview aggregates the admitted-turn recorder in Go SessionManager; the DraftStore remains process-local with an explicit standalone model adapter and no publication flow. Manager construction now owns one default typed DraftStore and injects it through common create/fork/ordinary and scheduled restoration, preserving fleet/owner/session quotas. New managers start empty pools; no draft is restored from SQL or transcripts. The separate typed candidate parser now checks exact five-field schema, recursive masking changes, create/skip semantics, strict integer/unique/in-range evidence and canonical skill validation in source order. It retains only immutable original fields and detached evidence; transient JSON boundary maps preserve last-wins duplicate keys and nonfinite-type outcomes without open domain payload. Native UTF-8/lone-surrogate refusal and safe masker panic errors are explicit. A separate typed SkillPreviewer now implements source projection/focus/masking, two attempts with safe repair reasons, provider/cancellation outcomes, post-parse health and owner/session-bound draft retention through an explicit model seam. Empty supplied ledgers cannot fall back to history; failed calls retain no draft. Fixed source system text and 2500 output tokens are part of the immutable request interface; no previous model response enters repair. JSON maps are transient closed boundaries. Standalone Session.PreviewPersonalSkill now serializes with core turns and uses normal cache/recovery/shared limiter/telemetry, empty tools and personal_skill_preview purpose; only text reply blocks are joined, without live history or token-meter ownership. Manager admission/lease binding and authenticated routes remain pending; standalone memory root and individual tool/auto activation are implemented. Checks are not atomic filesystem fencing.
